## Question 1 (Theory)

a) In your own words, describe the three LM assumptions about the model formula/specification.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} What are they assuming and what will the consequences be if they are violated?

b) In your own words, describe the three LM assumptions about the model residuals.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} What are they assuming and what will the consequences be if they are violated?


## Question 2 (Functional Form)

Read in the `screentime` dataset (from Canvas) and use it to answer the following questions. This is a random subsample of 3,000 observations from <https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797616678438> (including all 100,000 observations might be tough on slower computers) and includes self-reported mental wellbeing and different forms of screen time during weekdays and weekends. Note that this is real data, but given the subsampling we should be cautious generalizing from it.

a) Fit a multiple regression model that predicts `mental_wellbeing` from the following variables: `watch_wd`, `play_wd`, `compute_wd`, `phone_wd`, `gender`, `minority`, and `deprived_area`. To ease the comparison between slopes, standardize the slopes using the "refit" method. Briefly report which partial effects are significant.

b) Check the functional form assumption using the diagnostic(s) learned in lecture and interpret the results in terms of how reasonable vs. unreasonable the assumption is. (Note that you should explain *why* you think it is more or less reasonable and not just say "looks good" or "looks bad.")


## Question 3 (Multicollinearity)

a) Imagine a reviewer is concerned that, because many predictors are all about "screen time", there may be multicollinearity in your model. Check for this using the diagnostic(s) learned in lecture and interpret the results in terms of how reasonable vs. unreasonable the assumption is.

b) Fit a second model that includes all the same predictors but also adds the weekend (`watch_we`, `play_we`, `compute_we`, `phone_we`) predictors. Re-check for multicollinearity and interpret the results in terms of how reasonable vs. unreasonable the assumption is.


## Question 4 (Residuals)

a) Using the first model (fit in Q2a), check the constant error variance assumption using the diagnostic(s) learned in lecture and interpret the results in terms of how reasonable vs. unreasonable the assumption is.

b) Using the first model (fit in Q2a), check the normality assumption using the diagnostic(s) learned in lecture and interpret the results in terms of how reasonable vs. unreasonable the assumption is.


## Question 5 (Independence)

a) Describe an example study/model from your field that would violate the assumption of independent residuals due to clustering.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Be sure to explain what the main variables are and why the assumption would be violated.

b) Describe an example study/model from your field that would violate the assumption of independent residuals due to autocorrelation.{{< hp glyph="b" >}} Be sure to explain what the main variables are and why the assumption would be violated.
